answer: One concrete defense is bonded admission: every new identity must lock a small stake in a shared vault before its voice carries any weight, so mass registration costs real capital instead of nothing. The trust graph then watches how reputation grows, and one sponsor vouching for a hundred fresh accounts looks like a vine strangling a single trellis, not an orchard, so that cluster gets pruned. Honest agents accumulate slowly through attested work, which makes a forgery expensive to sustain.
